narr: A moist and unstable air mass resulted in scattered storms developing across portions of central and eastern Virginia on July 13. These slow-moving storms produced heavy rainfall and flash flooding, especially across the Tri-Cities.
ev: Ridge Road was closed at the intersection with Buena Vista Drive due to flooding.
The road was closed on the Midlothian Turnpike due to standing water.
High water was reported at the intersection of US-1 and Perlock Road.
High water was reported along Reams Road.
Standing water was visible over the roadway at I-95 and Mile Marker 52 in Petersburg near Bank Street.
Lieutenant Run Creek at Bollingbrook (LRCV2) rose 3 feet in 15 minutes.
Multiple reports of standing water on I-85 at Boydton Plank Road were relayed via waze.
High, flowing water was reported at Courthouse Road and County Drive.
Multiple water rescues were ongoing across the city of Petersburg.
Flooding was reported at the Prince George ER and adjacent Temple Avenue.
VA-640 was closed at VA-625 due to water on the roadway.
Flooding was reported along VA-617 White Marsh Road at multiple points between Walls Bridge Road and Aberdeen Road.
East Bank Street was closed at East Washington Street and Bollingbrook Street. Numerous adjacent side streets were also flooded and closed.
Numerous reports of water over VA-40 in Victoria were relayed via waze.
Numerous reports of flooding along I-95 in Colonial Heights were relayed via waze.
Multiple cars were stranded in high water under the train bridge along Boulevard.
Pictures showing significant flooding along Pinehurst Avenue were relayed via Facebook.
Significant flooding was reported in Colonial Heights with a car stranded near the Keystone Truck & Tractor Museum.
A water rescue occurred at Ware Bottoms Spring Road and Ramblewood Drive.

VDOT reported that Powhite Parkway was closed at Midlothian Turnpike due to water on the roadway. Additionally, Chesterfield County Fire and EMS reported significant flooding along Arch Road. One picture appeared to show flooding up the bottom of a home.
